title.narrative: Anolei Women Camel Milk Co-operative Limited and University of Greenwich

description.narrative: The project titled, "Adding value to camel milk value chain in Northern Kenya" partners with Anolei Women Camel Milk Co-operative to strengthen capacity for new value-added products and enhance productivity in camel milk production, collection and marketing. Innovation area – Value addition The KTP project aligns with the Anolei Women Camel Milk Co-operative’s aims to strengthen the capacity and livelihood security of women milk traders, by diversifying from primarily raw milk production and collection to a host of demand-driven value-added products. However, frequent milk spoilage and limited market reach have led to significant income and opportunity losses. The co-operative has identified the needs to strengthen capacity, in post-production technologies and business practices, while being cautious against the repeated instances of male appropriation when small enterprises become more lucrative and formalised. Recent research has shown that 2% of the total camel milk produced in Kenya gets to the urban markets, 10% in local markets and 38% domestic consumption, and rest 50% are lost at harvest or during postharvest handling. Majority of the losses takes place due to physiochemical and microbiological changes along the value chain. The proposed project will focus to reduce these losses by half at Anolei Women Camel Milk Co-operative within the project duration. Apart from management innovation, the technological interventions which the project intends to apply at the co-op include solar cooling and improved logistics. Moreover, the project will also focus to reduce the reliance on fossil fuels and incorporate renewable energy resources which will help reduce pollution. ODA – The introduction of value-added products and enhanced nutrition and health of camel will result in a significant financial payback to the cooperative and associated wider pastoralist community. By the end of the project, the capacity of the women co-operative will be increased by 7%, and over the next 5 years after the project, it is expected to further expand by 15%. Camel milk has a significant contribution towards livelihoods in the arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs) of Kenya. 83% area of Kenya falls under ASALs, and support one-third of its population. Subsistence pastoralists and smallholder farmers in ASALs experience and one of the highest poverty levels in the country with 74-97% people living below the poverty line. Camel milk contributes up to 40% of the pastoralist household income. Enhancing the safety and market for camel milk and its processed products would have a significant economic impact on the people living in ASALs. Camel milk is known to have a significant impact on pastoral capacities to cope and adapt to change. It represents a major source of income for pastoralist inhabiting in drylands of Africa, and Asia (including India). It is important to note that pastoral communities in Kenya are one of the most marginalized and impoverished groups. Moreover, they are disproportionately impacted by increased climate variability due to their dependence on forage, feed and other natural resources.
